accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Common Core State Standards ELA L.5.2c text (use a comma to set off the words yes and no, to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence, and to indicate direct address), the National Curriculum in England English Appendix 2 (Years 5 and 6: commas to clarify meaning or avoid ambiguity), and the Cambridge Grammar of the English Language on interjections, vocatives and interrogative tags. Every lab sentence was checked: vocatives are set off once at the edges and twice mid-sentence, no as a determiner (No dogs are allowed) and yes as a subject or object take no comma, and tag questions take a comma and a question mark.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: a comma after every name even a subject or object (step 1 Sam came to look, I gave Priya the book, Mum said it was late; prediction on Mum), half a pair for a mid-sentence name (step 2 prediction I think Mum that we are late; challenge I think, Mia you're right), a comma after no as a determiner (step 4 No dogs are allowed; challenge No, dogs allowed), splitting Thank you (step 2 gap feedback; challenge Thank, you Leo), and ending a tag question with a full stop (step 3 slot feedback; challenge).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagaddr is about setting off words outside the clause: the learner taps the person spoken to or Nobody, taps gap dots between word chips to place single and paired commas, drags comma and question-mark tokens into the two slots of a tag question, sorts yes/no/name sentences into needs a comma or no comma, and drags the name Zara to the start, middle and end of one sentence while placing the commas that follow it. lab_distinct kept it under 30% against flagambig, flagcomma, flagfront and every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The rules come out of the learner's own taps: tapping Mum in Mum said it was late returns 'Mum is in the sentence, but nobody is being spoken to'; tapping between Thank and you returns 'Thank you stays together. The comma goes before the name'; dropping a full stop before the tag returns 'A full stop here would end the sentence before the tag'; the move-the-name step shows one comma at the start, a pair in the middle and one at the end on the same words, and the done screen lists all three.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions hold the tempting wrong answer the step then disproves: that Mum in Mum said it was late needs a comma because it is a name, that I think Mum that we are late needs only one comma, and that No dogs are allowed here takes a comma after No. The done line repeats the learner's prediction against the answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve distinct wrong-answer messages: missing comma after a reply yes, stray comma inside the clause, Thank you split, missing comma before a name, the meaning flip in No, dogs allowed, a comma between subject and verb, a missing comma before a tag, a full stop on a tag question, the missing second comma after Mia, the missing first comma before Mia, and two messages for commas around yes used inside a sentence. Every wrong tap in the lab steps gets its own message too.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short with one rule each and worked examples (Put a comma before it and a question mark at the end: It's cold today, isn't it?) and pass the family readability limit; the adult text was rewritten into shorter sentences after the first validator run scored FK 13.1, and now passes. The adult text uses the precise terms interjection, direct address, vocative, tag question, subject, object and determiner sense of no.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases and the explanation stayed under the 12% six-word overlap limit against every lesson, including Commas to avoid ambiguity, Fronted Adverbials and Commas and Punctuating Direct Speech. Every feedback line names the word and the comma job involved.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (touch, light and dark) for every step after a wrong tap and after Show me: word chips wrap with room left for the gap dot at the end of a row (fixed after the first screenshot clipped the dot after pass), the tag slots sit beside the statement and tag, the sort card, feedback and bins no longer overlap (moved after the first screenshot), and the move-the-name holes show in blue for the target position.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every canvas action has a labelled button ('Sam is spoken to', 'Nobody is spoken to', 'Comma after Thank', 'Put a question mark in the slot', 'No dogs are allowed here: No comma', 'Put Zara at the middle'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback line.
